title: Utpala Dynasty
capsule: The Utpalas ruled Kashmir from 855, when Avantivarman founded the dynasty by displacing the Karkota line, until the early 11th century. Avantivarman's reign (855–883) was distinguished by the minister Suyya's large-scale hydraulic engineering works that reclaimed flood-prone land and revived agriculture. His successor Shankaravarman (883–902) pursued aggressive campaigns into the Punjab, imposing heavy taxation to fund them. The dynasty fragmented into competing claimants after c. 939, and effective Utpala rule over Kashmir ended by c. 1003 when the Lohara dynasty established itself.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty is attested primarily through the Rajatarangini chronicle of Kalhana (12th c.), whose chronology is broadly accepted but lacks independent corroboration for territorial extent.
